sources.entry: Blurt - Free, open-source dictation for macOS: hold a key, talk, and polished text lands in whatever app you're typing in. Powered by AssemblyAI speech-to-text (bring your own API key).

summary.one_liner: Blurt is a free, MIT-licensed native macOS dictation app that pastes AssemblyAI-transcribed, LLM-cleaned speech into whatever app has focus, using your own API key.
keywords: share voice notes into any app
type with my voice on mac
summary.what_it_does: Blurt records microphone audio while a single modifier key (right Command by default, or right Option or fn) is held or toggled, then sends it in one HTTPS POST to AssemblyAI's dictation API. That call returns transcription with server-side LLM cleanup, and Blurt pastes the result into the focused app via a synthesized Cmd+V, saving and restoring the prior clipboard. Users can supply custom style instructions (up to four), key vocabulary terms, and text shortcuts that expand phrases locally after the response. Context sent with each request is limited to recent in-session dictations and the text before the cursor, with a README-described privacy design. The repo also contains the BlurtEngine Swift package, which is documented as embeddable, and an in-development iPhone app and keyboard. A floating overlay shows mic level and pipeline phase, and Sparkle handles update checks.
use_cases: dictate text into any Mac app
voice typing in chat or documents
replace built-in macOS dictation with a faster option
build a custom dictation app on the BlurtEngine package
dictate code comments or terminal input by voice
how_to_run: Install Xcode 26+ (full Xcode, not just Command Line Tools), Homebrew, and an Apple Development certificate
notable: Single lone-modifier trigger with tap-to-toggle and hold-to-talk, and the event tap swallows no keystrokes
One HTTP request per utterance performs both transcription and LLM cleanup, with no local models
Context privacy: no app, window title, field, or selection is sent; password fields are never read
Dependency-free BlurtEngine Swift package with protocol seams, offered for embedding in other dictation apps
Optional synth cue sounds modeled on Yamaha DX7 and Roland Juno-106
caveats: Requires an AssemblyAI API key; audio and context are sent to AssemblyAI, so their privacy policy applies
macOS 15 or later is required; the Liquid Glass UI needs macOS 26
Building from source needs full Xcode 26+ and an Apple Development certificate
The iPhone app and keyboard are described as in development
